source.title: One-Time Soft Alignment Enables Resilient Learning without Weight Transport
source.authors: Jeonghwan Cheon; J. Bae; Se-Bum Paik

record.tranche_reason: The study reports test-accuracy outcomes for different feedback-learning schemes, but does not test the listed claim versions or measure the training–test gap they describe.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracy and Hessian results for its own initial-feedback-alignment method. It does not test random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, or the listed optimizer, batch-size, dropout, sharpness-gap, or memorized-example claims. No result directly measures a train–test gap.
record.test_reason: The BP baselines in Tables S1 and S2 provide incidental evidence for V3: CIFAR-10 test accuracy is 62.13% and 73.10% for two CNNs versus 53.32% for the fully connected network. These are separately configured benchmarks, not a controlled architectural ablation. The feedback-alignment and Hessian experiments do not test the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that one-time soft alignment improves feedback-alignment learning, stability, generalization, and robustness, while acknowledging an accuracy gap relative to BP in deeper or more complex models.
record.recipe_differences: The study changes the feedback pathway and initialization condition, comparing backpropagation, baseline feedback alignment, and initial feedback alignment. It does not use the claim versions' random-label, width-sweep, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or memorized-example procedures.
record.method_sensitivity: Initial alignment angle, dataset, architecture, network depth, training-data size, and weight-variance settings are reported as affecting outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Initial feedback alignment improves test accuracy over baseline FA and approaches BP in some settings, with remaining deficits in CNNs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: One-time alignment of forward and fixed feedback weights improves feedback-alignment learning.

fits_no_version.finding: Initial alignment changes Hessian curvature and loss-landscape geometry; the main text contains an inconsistent statement about angle direction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Stronger initial feedback alignment is associated with flatter converged loss landscapes.

record.problems: The paper states that a performance gap remains in deeper or more complex models. Many main-text outcomes are figure-based without numeric values in the text; table results report mean ± standard deviation across ten trials. No direct train–test-gap measurement is reported.
record.rows_left_out: The text describes additional figure-only test-accuracy comparisons across datasets, depth, training-set size, weight-variance settings, and alignment angles, plus corruption and adversarial robustness results. These do not measure a listed version and were omitted; detailed supplementary figure results are in Figures S4–S13.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-versus-random-label held-out performance under the same architecture and recipe.
Width beyond the interpolation threshold and its effect on test error.
Local connectivity as the explanation; learned sparse connections; initialization from trained CNNs; a controlled CNN-versus-fully-connected comparison holding the training recipe constant.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons and tuning-dependent differences.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout interventions, small-data exceptions, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, generalization-gap rankings, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal of memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

missing.what: Separate fully connected BP benchmark row: CIFAR-10 test accuracy 53.32 ± 0.27%, two 512-unit hidden layers. Benchmark training continues until test accuracy fails to improve for ten epochs.

Separate CNN BP benchmark rows: CIFAR-10 test accuracy 62.13 ± 0.90% for 2 Conv + 3 FC and 73.10 ± 0.29% for 5 Conv + 3 FC. CNN training uses Adam and weight decay 0.0001; record the stated learning rates and recipe differences.

record.verdict_notes: The absence of an explicit train–test-gap statistic does not exclude V3, which concerns held-out architectural performance. BP here describes backpropagation with Adam, not an SGD-versus-Adam comparison. The architectural evidence is incidental and confounded by recipe differences.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy on natural labels for the same architectures and recipes.
Width sweeps beyond the zero-training-error threshold and resulting test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-model generalization under the comparisons specified.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization under the tuning conditions specified.
Large versus small batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
The effects of adding or removing dropout and weight decay under the specified regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of train–test gaps; the study reports Hessian metrics but does not measure that gap or the stated perturbation measure.
Removing the most memorized training examples and comparing the effect with removing random examples.

rows.operation_detail: Measured Hessian trace and largest eigenvalue across initial-alignment conditions.
rows.value: Both metrics decrease as the initial alignment angle increases, then plateau beyond a certain alignment threshold.
rows.note: This is a curvature result; the paper does not relate a magnitude-aware perturbation measure to measured train–test gaps.
rows.check: Hessian trace and largest eigenvalue are not V7's magnitude-aware sharpness or its ranking of generalization gaps. Section 4.3 says curvature decreases with increasing angle, but A.3.3 says it decreases with decreasing angle; flag this internal directional inconsistency.

relationships.condition: Separately configured CIFAR-10 BP benchmarks: fully connected network versus LeNet- and AlexNet-variant CNNs.
relationships.reason: Based on text/table results requiring the missing BP rows: CNN accuracies are 62.13% and 73.10%, versus 53.32% for the fully connected network. Different training configurations prevent isolating architecture as the cause.
relationships.display_finding: The reported higher LeNet-variant and AlexNet-variant accuracies remain unverified across separately configured backpropagation benchmarks.
